summary:
H.R. 2866, the "No Visas for Anti-Semitic Students Act," introduced in the 119th Congress (1st Session) by Ms. Malliotakis and referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary, directs the Secretary of State to revoke or deny student visas to aliens determined to have engaged in antisemitic conduct.

Section 2(a) mandates that the Secretary of State revoke or deny a visa under subparagraph (F) (academic students) or (M) (vocational students) of section 101(a)(15) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(15)) to any alien who, on or after the date of enactment, both (1) engages in "prohibited antisemitic conduct" and (2) is determined by the Secretary, pursuant to INA § 237(a)(4)(C)(i) (8 U.S.C. 1227(a)(4)(C)(i)) (the foreign-policy deportability ground), to pose potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences for the United States through such conduct. Both conditions are prerequisites, and the provision applies prospectively (conduct occurring on or after enactment).

Section 2(b) defines "antisemitism" by reference to the definition adopted May 26, 2016, by the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA), as adopted by the Department of State, including its "contemporary examples of antisemitism." "Prohibited antisemitic conduct" is defined as (A) engaging in a physical act of violence, vandalism, or harassment targeting a Jewish individual, their property, a community institution, or religious facility, with intent to intimidate or harm based on Jewish identity or affiliation; or (B) providing material support (including funding, organizing, or inciting) to a person knowing that the person intended to use such support to engage in conduct described in subparagraph (A).

Section 3 amends INA § 214 (8 U.S.C. 1184) by adding a new subsection (s). Paragraph (s)(1) bars an alien from being granted or maintaining F or M nonimmigrant status where the alien engages in prohibited antisemitic conduct and the Secretary makes the § 237(a)(4)(C)(i) foreign-policy determination. Paragraph (s)(2) requires the Secretary to revoke the visa of an alien already in F or M status upon determining that the alien engaged in prohibited antisemitic conduct and that the alien or conduct poses potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences. Paragraph (s)(3) incorporates definitions parallel to those in Section 2(b).

The bill contains no separate effective-date provision (taking effect upon enactment), no authorization of appropriations, and no sunset. The operative revocation/denial obligations are cast as mandatory ("shall").
